citation.title: Topology Optimisation under Uncertainties with Neural Networks
citation.authors: Martin Eigel, Marvin Haase, Johannes Neumann

included.physics: linear elasticity with uncertain loads and stiffness

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For the deterministic bridge, CNN-assisted optimization converged in 441 iterations versus 538 for the classical optimizer and used less total time.
claim.location: Section 4.1.3, Table 1; times repeated in Table 4
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Table 4, first load: classical Algorithm A1 4 min 43 s / CNN Algorithm 1 4 min 05 s = 283/245 = 1.1551 [inferred].
claim.alternatives: Abstract and conclusion describe faster optimization qualitatively; Table 4 gives more load cases and LSTM timings; Section 4.1.4 compares stochastic cases.

baseline.classical_method: phase-field gradient optimization, Algorithm A1 (Sections 2 and 4; Appendix A)
baseline.implementation: FEniCS finite-element simulations, reference optimizer in linked public repository (Section 4; introduction)
baseline.hardware_classical: WIAS computing infrastructure/cluster mentioned, specifications not stated (Section 4.1.4; acknowledgments)
baseline.hardware_ml: WIAS computing infrastructure/cluster mentioned, specifications not stated (Section 4.1.4; acknowledgments)
baseline.problem_size: 2D bridge, adaptively refined mesh up to at least 15,000 vertices (Section 4.1.3)
baseline.classical_iterations: 538 to convergence for primary deterministic load (Table 1)
baseline.classical_time: 4 min 43 s for primary deterministic load (Table 4)
baseline.ml_time: 4 min 05 s for CNN Algorithm 1, primary deterministic load (Table 4)
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; Section 4.1.1 describes generating sample paths with Algorithm A1
baseline.quality_metric: FE-computed compliance and objective J, plus phase-field volume constraint (Table 1; Appendix A.1)
baseline.quality_gap: For the primary load, compliance 1173.22 classical versus 1148.66 CNN; objective 1475.39 versus 1206.49 (Table 1)

R1.evidence: Table 1: CNN returns lower compliance than classical at a common nominal volume constraint (Appendix A.1), but achieved physical-field volume and a matched-quality timing protocol are not given.

R2.evidence: Sections 4.1.3-4.1.4 and Table 4: no text establishes a GPU/CPU mismatch, an excessive fixed iteration count, or a slow per-iteration classical solver relative to a strong baseline.

R3.evidence: Section 4.1.1 describes classical optimization runs to generate training paths; Tables 1 and 4 report optimization runtimes, but neither data-generation nor training cost or amortization is reported.

R4.evidence: Tables 1-4 compute compliance through the FE optimization; Appendix A.1 states the volume constraint; Section 4.1.4 describes collapsed designs, but no failure rate or achieved physical volume is reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: 5 deterministic loads in Table 4; stochastic bridge with 224 samples per optimization iteration in Table 2 (Appendix A.2)

notes: Section 4.1.3 states ten repeats with averaging for runtime only. Section 4.1.4 sets seed 42 for stochastic comparison. The linked public repository contains optimizer and experiment code. Data Availability Statement says not applicable, although code to generate data is linked.
